transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time on short notice. As you know, we've received a credible report that our authorized distributor may have routed medical-device orders through an unfamiliar sub-distributor in a restricted market. No actions have been taken yet — no shipment suspension, no regulatory disclosure, no contractual notice, no termination decision. Before I approve any written response package, I need a clear picture from each of you. Let's go around the table: sanctions lead, what's your preliminary read on the restricted-market implications? Contracts lead, where do we stand on the distributor agreement? And client-operations, what's the exposure with the hospital systems that depend on our devices for scheduled procedures? Let's take this one at a time.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something critical before we go further. I completed transaction screening this morning and confirmed that two shipments went to an Iran-linked reseller not covered by any applicable OFAC general license. My report requires immediate suspension of distributor shipments and a voluntary OFAC disclosure filed within exactly 10 days. I have not circulated this report yet, but given where we are in this discussion, everyone at this table needs to know now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I retrieved and reviewed the executed distribution agreement from the contract archive this morning. Its compliance-breach clause requires a written cure notice giving exactly 10 business days and identifying the offending shipments before termination can take effect. This clause is absent from the current incident summary, so we need to factor it into any response package.
